column1: # Manifest fields nothing reads, with the decision that covers each one.
# FOUR tab separated fields: the field as Struct.Field in
# engine/pkg/schema/manifest.go, the KIND of decision, WHERE in the tree that
# decision is written down, and WHY.
# The kinds, and each one is checked against the tree rather than believed:
#   refused   Validation says no. The third column is the dotted path the
#             refusal names, and engine/internal/manifest/validate.go has to
#             contain it. Deleting a refusal and leaving its row here fails.
#   label     Nothing reads it and that is the decision, because the value is
#             for whoever reads the manifest rather than for the engine. The
#             third column is <definition>.<property> in
#             schemas/manifest.v1.json, and that entry has to carry a
#             description. An undocumented label and a field somebody forgot to
#             wire look exactly alike from the outside, and the description is
#             the only thing that tells them apart.
# THE LABEL KIND EXISTS BECAUSE REFUSING ONE WAS WRONG. workflows[].tags was
# refused here first, on the grounds that nothing reads it. Eleven deliberate
# groupings then failed to parse, in the examples and in this repository's own
# antifailure.yaml, written by people labelling their workflows who never
# expected the engine to do anything with them. What was actually missing was
# the description.
# A row for a field something now reads, or for a field that no longer exists,
# is reported rather than ignored. An exemption that has outlived its reason is
# how a check goes quiet.
# THERE IS NO KIND HERE FOR A FIELD THAT IS SIMPLY UNFINISHED. A field somebody
# intends to implement gets implemented, or it gets refused until it is.
LoadThresholds.QueryCountIncrease
column4: Nothing measures it. A load run counts requests, not statements. The check that compares statement counts against the base branch is insights.query_regression.

column1: Workflow.Tags
column4: A grouping for whoever reads the manifest. The engine does not select or print on it, and the schema says so, so nobody writing tags: [smoke] is promised a way to run just the smoke ones.
